long_biography.plain_text:
Larry A. Silverstein grew up in Brooklyn and entered real estate through the brokerage run by his father, Harry. He worked there while studying at New York University. In 1957 he joined his father and brother-in-law Bernard Mendik in buying their first Manhattan building. The venture developed into Silverstein Properties. When the partnership ended in the 1970s, Silverstein continued acquiring and developing commercial property through the firm he founded.

Silverstein built the private company into an owner, developer and manager of office, residential, hotel and mixed-use property. Its best-known work is the redevelopment of the World Trade Center site, where Silverstein secured a long lease and led development of several new towers. He remains the company's chairman, while a later generation leads day-to-day operations. His fortune reflects equity and partnership interests in the business. Project costs, building values, lease obligations, insurance proceeds, lender capital and assets held by project entities are not his personal wealth.
